fullPassage: Various factors are behind the cognitive bias towards coherence. One is the extrapolation of past experience that influences our perceptions through expectations about what we are going to perceive. A case in point here is the well-known playing-card experiment involving impossible cards. A subject is briefly shown a variety of playing cards, some of which are doctored (such as a black king of hearts) and is asked to identify them. In the majority of cases, the subjects did not note the unusual features of the doctored cards, but rather perceived them as regular cards. The black king of hearts would thus be identified as a king of spades — not because the subject cannot differentiate heart-shapes from spade-shapes, but because he sees what he is expecting to see, namely a regular playing card. Our expectations about what we are going to perceive can strongly influence what we do in fact perceive. In this way, having perceived various coherent phenomena in the past, we can expect that future perceived phenomena are similarly coherent, and this expectation may make it more likely that we in fact experience them as coherent, whether they are coherent or not.

One is the extrapolation of past experience that influences our perceptions through expectations about what we are going to perceive. A case in point here is the well-known playing-card experiment involving impossible cards. A subject is briefly shown a variety of playing cards, some of which are doctored (such as a black king of hearts) and is asked to identify them. In the majority of cases, the subjects did not note the unusual features of the doctored cards, but rather perceived them as regular cards. The black king of hearts would thus be identified as a king of spades — not because the subject cannot differentiate heart-shapes from spade-shapes, but because he sees what he is expecting to see, namely a regular playing card. Our expectations about what we are going to perceive can strongly <u>influence</u> what we do in fact perceive. In this way, having perceived various coherent phenomena in the past, we can expect that future perceived phenomena are similarly coherent, and this expectation may make it more likely that we in fact experience them as coherent, whether they are coherent or not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>influence</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① affect(영향을 미치다): influence의 유의어
❌ ② shape(형성하다): influence의 유의어
✅ ③ neglect(무시하다): influence의 반의어로 가장 적절 ←정답
❌ ④ determine(결정하다): influence의 유의어

questions.passage:

questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 feature의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: extrapolation = 외삽, 추정 (알려진 정보를 확장하여 미지의 것을 추정하는 행위)
det.analysis:
❌ ① perception(인식): 감각을 통한 인식 행위로, 정의와 불일치
❌ ② coherence(일관성): 논리적 연결을 뜻하는 말로, 정의와 불일치
✅ ③ extrapolation(외삽): 알려진 정보를 확장하여 미지의 것을 추정하는 행위라는 정의에 정확히 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ expectation(기대): 미래에 대한 기대를 뜻하며, '확장 추정'이라는 정의와 불일치

questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

perceive → ____

det.korean: 피험자들은 조작된 카드의 특이한 특징을 알아채지 못하고 오히려 보통 카드로 '인식했다'.
det.analysis: 주어 the subjects + 과거시제 문맥(did not note와 병렬) → 동사 perceive를 과거형 perceived로 변환. but rather perceived them as regular cards가 문맥상 자연스러움.

questions.passage: In this way, having perceived various coherent phenomena in the past, we can expect that future perceived phenomena are similarly coherent, and this __________ (expect) may make it more likely that we in fact experience them as coherent.

expect → ____

det.korean: 이런 식으로, 과거에 다양한 일관된 현상을 인식한 결과 이 '기대'가 실제로 일관되게 경험하게 만들 수 있다.
det.analysis: this + 빈칸 → 명사 필요. 지시형용사 this 뒤에 명사가 와야 하므로 동사 expect를 명사형 expectation으로 변환. this expectation may make it more likely가 문맥상 자연스러움.
det.tip: expect(동사: 기대하다) → expectation(명사: 기대). this 뒤에는 명사 필수
